preconditions.expression: len(hamming_distances) == 3 and len(hamming_distances[0]) == 3 and len(hamming_distances[1]) == 2 and len(hamming_distances[2]) == 1
preconditions.description: Input consists of three lines with the correct number of Hamming distances.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(d, int) and 0 <= d <= 100000 for d in [hamming_distances[0][0], hamming_distances[0][1], hamming_distances[0][2], hamming_distances[1][0], hamming_distances[1][1], hamming_distances[2][0]])
preconditions.description: All Hamming distances are integers between 0 and 100000.

preconditions.expression: any(d > 0 for d in [hamming_distances[0][0], hamming_distances[0][1], hamming_distances[0][2], hamming_distances[1][0], hamming_distances[1][1], hamming_distances[2][0]])
preconditions.description: At least one Hamming distance is positive.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or (len(return_value.splitlines()) == 5 and len(return_value.splitlines()[0]) == 1 and all(len(s) == int(return_value.splitlines()[0]) for s in return_value.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: Output is either '-1' or consists of five lines where the first line is the length of the strings and the next four lines are the strings of that length.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or all(s in {'a', 'b'} for s in ''.join(return_value.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: If output is not '-1', all characters in the strings are either 'a' or 'b'.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or all(sum(1 for i in range(int(return_value.splitlines()[0])) if return_value.splitlines()[i+1][j] != return_value.splitlines()[k+1][j]) == hamming_distances[i][k] for i in range(3) for k in range(i+1, 4))
postconditions.description: If output is not '-1', the Hamming distances between the output strings match the input Hamming distances.
